title: A HARD DAY IN THE CAMP

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he said to them, 'This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: "Each man strap a sword to his side. Go back and forth through the camp from one end to the other, each killing his brother and friend and neighbour."' The Levites did as Moses commanded, and that day about three thousand of the people died." - Exod 32:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard passage, and we should not soften it. Three thousand people died that day.

We must read it honestly and in its setting. Israel had just entered a covenant with God as a nation, sworn at Sinai. Idolatry was not a private matter of taste; it was national treason against the covenant King, and this was a unique moment in redemptive history under a theocracy that no longer exists. This is a historical account, not a pattern for anyone today. Nowhere does the New Testament permit violence in the name of God. Our weapons are not of this world (2 Cor 10:4), and Jesus explicitly told Peter to put his sword away (John 18:11).

What this passage does show us, unavoidably, is that God takes sin seriously. Far more seriously than we do. The wages of sin is death (Rom 6:23) — that is not an Old Testament idea; it is the whole Bible's verdict.

Which makes the cross all the more astonishing. At Sinai, three thousand died because of sin. At Pentecost, three thousand were saved (Acts 2:41). The judgement we deserved fell on Christ instead. If you have ever wondered whether God is serious about sin, look at Calvary. And if you have ever wondered whether He is serious about mercy — look at the same place.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat sin as lightly as your culture does?
2. What does the cross tell you about the seriousness of your sin?
3. How does God's justice make His mercy more precious to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, I see how serious sin is. Thank You that Jesus bore what I deserved. Amen.
